classification.difficultyReason: Count shapes and coloured subsets, then divide both terms by their highest common factor.

content.prompt: For the diagram opposite, write down the following ratios. Express all ratios in simplest form.

spec.description: Three rows of three right triangles followed by two circles. Triangle vertices are top-left, bottom-left and bottom-right. Each row's first triangle is blue-filled. The first circle is blue-filled in the top two rows only. All other shapes are white. Ordinary outlines use house black.
spec.mathematics: 9 triangles, 6 circles; 2 blue circles and 4 white circles; 3 blue triangles and 6 white triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: All shapes and semantic fills are permanent givens; no answers are drawn.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the ratio of the number of triangles to the number of circles

answer.worked:
There are 9 triangles and 6 circles. Divide both terms by 3.
$$\begin{align*}\text{triangles}:\text{circles}&=9:6\\\text{triangles}:\text{circles}&=3:2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the ratio of the number of blue circles to the number of white circles

answer.worked:
There are 2 blue circles and 4 white circles. Divide both terms by 2.
$$\begin{align*}\text{blue circles}:\text{white circles}&=2:4\\\text{blue circles}:\text{white circles}&=1:2\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: the ratio of the number of blue triangles to the number of white triangles

answer.worked:
There are 3 blue triangles and 6 white triangles. Divide both terms by 3.
$$\begin{align*}\text{blue triangles}:\text{white triangles}&=3:6\\\text{blue triangles}:\text{white triangles}&=1:2\end{align*}$$
